card.keepWhy: The strongest one in the forest still asked for help.
sources: Bhagavata Purana, book 8, chapter 2 (Gajendra, king of the elephants, enters a lotus lake; a crocodile seizes his leg; the long struggle; his herd cannot free him)
Bhagavata Purana, book 8, chapters 3-4 (Gajendra’s prayer; he lifts a lotus in his trunk, 8.3.32; Vishnu comes on Garuda and frees him)
The film’s note: Gajendra’s prayer is still recited by many Hindus in hard times
Gajendra: gaja (elephant) + indra (chief, king); Gajanana taught in “How Ganesha got his head”
check: “A thousand years” of struggle (Bhagavata 8.2.29 is usually cited); confirm the verse.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? trying to fix something all on your own? it’s not working, and asking feels hard.
options: then this one is for you. listen.
then you’ll know this feeling. listen.
good. keep this one for when you need it.

steps.line: Gajendra was the king of the elephants, huge and strong. One day he waded into a lotus lake to drink.
Suddenly, a crocodile clamped onto his leg.

steps.q: His whole herd is there with him. Can they pull him free?
o: Yes, together they haul him out
They try, and in the end they can’t
They run when the crocodile appears
steps.why: They try, and fail. In the Bhagavata, even his mates and his herd can’t pull him free. Watch how long it goes on.

steps.line: He pulled. The crocodile pulled. His herd tried to help, and gave up. The story says it went on for a thousand years.

steps.q: He’s still stuck, after all those years. What do you think Gajendra does?
o: Gathers himself for one last pull
Lets go, and sinks under, worn out
Lifts a lotus and calls out to Vishnu
steps.why: He stops fighting alone, and asks. Watch who comes.

steps.line: Finally, exhausted, Gajendra stopped fighting alone. He lifted a single lotus to the sky, and called out to Vishnu.

steps.q: In the Bhagavata Purana, how does an elephant know the words to call on Vishnu?
o: He remembers a prayer from a past life
His herd had taught him the words
He doesn’t use words, only the lotus
steps.why: The Bhagavata says Gajendra had been a king, Indradyumna, in a past life, and an old prayer came back to him. Many Hindus still recite it, the Gajendra Stuti, in hard times.

steps.line: And Vishnu came, flying on his great eagle, Garuda, and set him free.

steps.q: Vishnu frees Gajendra with his spinning discus. What becomes of the crocodile?
o: It dies, and that’s the end of it
It’s freed too, from an old curse
It’s banished to the lake’s bottom
steps.why: In the Bhagavata, the crocodile was a heavenly singer named Huhu, cursed by a sage. Vishnu’s discus set both of them free at once.

steps.line: Even the strongest one in the forest needed help. Asking was the turning point.
steps.label: today

steps.q: In his prayer, Gajendra doesn’t ask to be saved from the jaws. What does he say he wants?
o: To live, and lead his herd again
To be freed from ignorance itself
That his herd be kept safe from harm
steps.why: In the Bhagavata (8.3.25) he says he has no wish to go on living as an elephant; he asks to be freed from the ignorance that covers him. Many teachers read it as asking for the deepest help, not the nearest.

say: here’s what i love. gajendra was the strongest one in the forest, and he still needed help.
his turning point isn’t a bigger pull. it’s the moment he stops fighting alone and calls out. many hindus still recite his prayer in hard times.

steps.q: Many teachers read the story as a picture of every life. If Gajendra is the soul, what is the crocodile?
o: The world’s grip: time, death, clinging
Other people who wish you harm
The body, which the soul must leave
steps.why: In many readings the lake is the world and the crocodile its grip, which no strength breaks alone. And remember: even the crocodile was set free.

today.say: what have you been trying to fix alone? ask one person for help today. many hindus recite gajendra’s prayer in hard times. you can listen to it, say a short prayer of your own, or simply ask. it’s your choice.
options: that’s your lotus moment. lift it.
it was for him too, after a thousand years. one small ask.
